subtopic: ONNX / Interchange format vs high-performance runtime
learningObjective: Understand the boundary between ONNX as a model interchange format and the runtimes that consume it, avoiding the assumption that interchange = high performance.
stem: Which statements about ONNX as a model interchange format are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: ONNX defines a portable representation of a model (operators, initializers, shapes, versions); it does not itself define how to execute the model efficiently on any specific hardware — that is the job of ONNX-consuming runtimes (ONNX Runtime, TensorRT, OpenVINO, IREE, etc.).

Two runtimes consuming the same ONNX model can produce different latency/throughput because their operator implementations, fusion policies, kernel selection, and memory management are runtime-specific, even though the numerical results should match within spec tolerance.
Because ONNX is a widely adopted format, exporting a model to ONNX automatically guarantees it will be as fast on any target as the fastest hand-tuned implementation for that hardware.
ONNX bundles a specific execution engine into the model file; loading an `.onnx` file automatically brings in a runtime and there is no distinction between the format and its executors.

explanation: ONNX is an interchange format: it standardizes serialization, opset semantics, and shape/type info so a model produced by framework X can be consumed by runtime Y. It does not prescribe performance; different runtimes make different choices about kernel implementation, fusion, layout, and memory. C is a common misconception: interchange ≠ 'guaranteed maximum performance'. D is also wrong: an `.onnx` file is a data file; the runtime is separate.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: ONNX = interchange spec; execution is runtime-specific.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: same ONNX, different runtimes → different performance.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: interchange format does not imply peak performance.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: ONNX file does not embed a runtime.

nonImplications: Does not imply ONNX and downstream compilers (TensorRT, OpenVINO) do not share optimization work.
Does not imply ONNX is the only interchange format; StableHLO, GGUF, TorchScript serve different niches.

distractorRationales.D: Wrong claim that runtime is bundled.
